Yes, so many places it is absurd (at least in the context of leading theories.)

  • Proton Radius Puzzle - Basically we had the radius of the proton predicted perfectly by theory until about 2010, then we found a way to make a better measurement and it turns out the entire theory (the standard model) has to be scrapped because there's no way to make it fit the actual proton radius.

  • Proton Spin Crisis - Again, basically just invalidates the standard model (at least, everything relating to quarks) and was found in 1987. Some recent research suggests ways to patch this with angular momentum of quarks - but that's kind of irrelevant since the standard model cannot be right due to the first item in this list.

  • Why time exists is another big one - or rather, why we move in 1 direction through it. Though this one might come down to something stupid like "when the big bang happened we got blown forward in time and an object in motion stays in motion" because we still don't have even a hint of a clue what could make things go in only 1 direction.

  • Locality vs realism is another major one, in that to resolve some of the issues in quantum mechanics we have to either give up locality (i.e. things must have variables outside of reality as we know it for them to function as observed) or realism (i.e. if nothing exists until observed and the universe is basically in our imaginations.)

  • Quantum mechanics and relativity cannot be reconciled - This basically tells us one of or both of them are flat out wrong, because mathematically there is no way to make them mesh with eachother.

  • Inflation - Nobody really knows why it's happening at all, space is essentially being created everywhere.

  • Horizon problem - The big bang theory suggests there should be differences in different parts of the sky when we look back far enough, but it all looks the same.

  • Dark matter is basically a "we don't know why our theories are wrong so let's throw some variable in there called 'dark matter' to hold the space for the missing part of the equation." Then of course rather than correcting the equation we aim to look for "dark matter," which by definition is unobservable. Smart.

  • Dark energy basically the same issue as dark matter, only dealing with expansion of space instead of the rotation of galaxies.

  • The axis of evil is an issue where a bunch of the universe is aligned with our solar system (but only the really far > 13 billion light year stuff, not anything closer) - so either we're the center of the universe or some weird shit is going down.

I'll stop there without getting into the subatomic issues - because frankly the list could go on through several weeks of typing and that first point nullifies them all as "stupid questions" anyway.
